The extracted evidence establishes that ManyChat operates in the software sector [P2] (current profile, undated) and that, on a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16', the company states 140,000+ bots and 500M messages [S1, S2], with a separate slide stating 500M messages/month [S3]. These figures are consistent with a platform model serving a large number of bot-deploying users, but no revenue model, pricing structure, customer definition, or growth driver is found in the extracted evidence. How the company monetises, who pays, and what drives expansion are not found in the extracted evidence. Information Readiness Score: 12/100 Present: • Stage designation: Series A [P1] • Sector designation: Software [P2] • Traction figures (self-reported, unverified): 140,000+ bots [S1], 500M messages / 500M messages/month [S2, S3] • Funding raised figure (narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt, unverified): $23.1M [C1, S4] Needs Validation: • Message-volume measurement basis: total vs. per-month [C2, C3] requires clarification • Funding raised: no external source confirmed the $23.1M figure (per Pitch Deck Hunt) [C1] • All traction figures: no independent verification of bots or message counts • Revenue, burn rate, and cash position: not present • Team and founder credentials: not present • Product description and problem statement: not present • Market size and competitive landscape: not present • Use of proceeds: not present • Risk factors: not present Next evidence to supply: Audited or accountant-reviewed financials showing revenue, gross margin, and a dated cash balance with monthly burn rate would most immediately expand what can be assessed. Supported Points The company states 140,000+ bots as of a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1]; while unverified, this self-reported figure provides a reference point for platform adoption scale. Pitch Deck Hunt lists a cumulative funding figure of $23.1M raised [C1, S4]; although this could not be confirmed against independent evidence, it indicates the company has sought to characterise a meaningful prior capital history. Open Concerns The two message-volume figures — 500M messages (no interval stated) on the 'Traction by Apr-16' slide [S2] and 500M messages/month on a separate slide [S3] — use different measurement bases and have not been reconciled. Until clarified, it is unknown whether these refer to the same or different metrics, which is central to understanding actual usage scale. No revenue, burn rate, or dated cash balance is found in the extracted evidence, making it impossible to assess financial sustainability, capital efficiency, or how long reported funding would sustain operations. No team information is found in the extracted evidence; the experience and track record of the founders cannot be evaluated from available material. The $23.1M raised figure is narrated by Pitch Deck Hunt rather than stated in the body of the deck [C1, S4] and could not be confirmed against any independent source, leaving the actual funding history unestablished. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece of evidence is a dated income statement and cash flow statement showing revenue, gross margin, and monthly burn — these would allow assessment of whether the self-reported usage metrics translate into a financially sustainable business and would establish how much of the narrated $23.1M raised (per Pitch Deck Hunt) remains available.
